domain: Computer Science / Distributed Systems / Cloud Infrastructure / Container Orchestration
subject: Kubernetes

source_policy.preservation_rule: Preserve meaningful concepts, architecture, mechanisms, relationships, historical context, examples, distinctions, security model, APIs, workloads, storage, networking, criticisms, references and source-specific claims. Do not flatten relationships into generic related_to edges.

relationship_model.principle: Relationships are first-class objects. Each relationship records what connects two concepts, how the connection works, conditions, direction, effects, inverse/converse where meaningful, context, scope, source provenance and mathematical/formal representation where applicable.
central_system_model: human/client intent → Kubernetes API server → API objects → etcd persistent state → scheduler/controllers/watchers → nodes → kubelet/CRI/runtime → Pods/containers → observed state → status/API → reconciliation
Service → selector → Pod set → stable IP/DNS → load balancing
CRD → Custom Resource → Custom Controller → Operator behavior
Node heartbeat → failure detection → controller reconciliation → replacement workload

nodes.label: Declarative vs imperative orchestration
nodes.description: Kubernetes primarily represents desired state as objects; controllers determine corrective actions rather than requiring users to script every individual machine operation.

nodes.description: Container is the runtime unit; Pod is the Kubernetes deployable unit that groups one or more containers.

nodes.label: ReplicaSet vs Deployment

nodes.label: Stateful vs stateless workloads

relationships.mechanism: Kubernetes coordinates containerized workloads across machines through an API, control plane, node agents, schedulers and controllers.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Manual orchestration without control loops

relationships.mechanism: Kubernetes treats multiple machines as one orchestrated cluster resource domain.
relationships.effect: Pools machines into a managed execution environment.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Cluster can be operated without Kubernetes

relationships.mechanism: Control-plane components declare, schedule, reconcile and communicate desired workload state to worker nodes.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Nodes execute workloads while control plane coordinates

relationships.mechanism: API server validates requests and updates API-object state stored persistently in etcd.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: etcd does not replace API validation

relationships.mechanism: etcd stores the cluster state, including declarations such as desired Pod counts.
relationships.effect: Provides durable source-of-record state for API objects.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Observed runtime state remains distinct

relationships.mechanism: The API is declarative: clients submit objects describing desired outcomes.
relationships.effect: Clients state what should exist rather than manually orchestrating each machine.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Imperative tools can still be used to construct declarations

relationships.mechanism: spec records desired resource state.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: status records current state

relationships.mechanism: status records current state and is actively updated by controllers.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: spec is desired, not observed

relationships.mechanism: Controllers continuously reason about the difference between what is declared and what exists.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: No difference means convergence

relationships.mechanism: Controller observes cluster state and creates/updates/deletes resources to reduce divergence from desired state.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Actual state may change again after reconciliation

relationships.mechanism: Controllers communicate through the Kubernetes API to observe and modify managed resources.
relationships.effect: Decouples controllers from direct node manipulation.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Direct node mutation bypasses declarative API semantics

relationships.mechanism: The API server is the shared interface through which controllers observe and mutate API resources.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Controller implementations can be custom

relationships.mechanism: Scheduler chooses a node for an unscheduled Pod based on capacity and constraints.
relationships.effect: Binds workload demand to infrastructure supply.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: A Pod already assigned to a node is not newly scheduled

relationships.mechanism: Scheduler matches requested resources and policies against available node resources.
relationships.effect: Prevents placement exceeding available resources under scheduler rules.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Resource supply changes as workloads start/stop

relationships.mechanism: Affinity/anti-affinity policies constrain scheduler placement decisions.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Without constraints scheduler has broader placement choices

relationships.mechanism: Data locality can constrain placement to improve proximity to needed data.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Not all workloads require locality

relationships.mechanism: Quality-of-service is among the policy inputs considered by the scheduler.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Policy effect depends on scheduler configuration

relationships.mechanism: kubelet starts, stops and maintains containers organized into Pods according to control-plane direction.
relationships.effect: Realizes Pod state on a node.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: kubelet does not replace higher-level controllers

relationships.mechanism: kubelet sends periodic node-status heartbeats to the API server.
relationships.effect: Makes node health observable to control-plane logic.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Lost heartbeat can indicate failure

relationships.mechanism: Absence/change in node status allows the control plane to detect node failure.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Detection depends on status reporting

relationships.mechanism: A higher-level controller can observe node failure and create replacement Pods on healthy nodes.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Recovery requires healthy capacity and appropriate controller

relationships.mechanism: kubelet communicates with the container runtime through CRI.
relationships.effect: Separates Kubernetes node logic from runtime implementation.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Runtime implementation can vary

relationships.mechanism: CRI allows Kubernetes to support different container runtimes without hard-coding runtime implementation into kubelet.
relationships.effect: Enables runtime choice and ecosystem interoperability.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Specific runtime features may differ

relationships.mechanism: Container runtime manages lifecycle operations such as launching, reconciling and killing containers.
relationships.effect: Turns workload definitions into running container processes.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Runtime alone does not provide cluster-level scheduling

relationships.mechanism: kube-proxy implements proxy/load-balancing behavior supporting the Service abstraction.
relationships.effect: Routes traffic toward appropriate backend Pods.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Service abstraction remains separate from individual Pod identity

relationships.mechanism: Service membership is determined by label selector matching.
relationships.effect: Creates a stable backend set despite Pod churn.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Changing labels can change membership

relationships.mechanism: Service provides stable IP address and DNS name independent of individual Pod lifecycle.
relationships.effect: Clients target stable identity while backend Pods change.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Service identity differs from Pod IP

relationships.mechanism: Service distributes connections among matching Pods.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Distribution policy can vary with implementation/configuration

relationships.mechanism: Kubernetes DNS provides Service discovery through stable names.
relationships.effect: Clients can resolve Services without tracking Pod IPs.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: DNS is one of two discovery modes in source

relationships.mechanism: Namespaces divide resources into distinct collections for teams, projects and environments.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Namespace is not complete security isolation by itself

relationships.mechanism: A Pod groups one or more containers that are co-located on the same node and share context.
relationships.effect: Creates the basic deployable unit and local container context.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: A Pod can contain multiple containers but common use is one

relationships.mechanism: Each Pod receives a unique cluster IP according to the source.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Pod IP is not stable across Pod replacement

relationships.mechanism: Higher-level workload abstractions let users declare and manage groups of Pods rather than individual Pods.
relationships.effect: Raises management abstraction above individual containers.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Pods remain the execution unit

relationships.mechanism: ReplicaSet reconciles matching Pods to maintain the specified number of replicas.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Changing desired replicas changes target count

relationships.mechanism: ReplicaSet selector identifies the Pods it manages.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Incorrect selectors can cause management conflicts

relationships.mechanism: Deployment manages ReplicaSets and controls rollout/rollback behavior.
relationships.effect: Enables controlled application version changes and rollback.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: ReplicaSet still handles replica count

relationships.mechanism: Deployment controller changes ReplicaSet declarations to roll out updates.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Rollback can reverse rollout

relationships.mechanism: Deployment manages rollback of ReplicaSet/application state.
relationships.effect: Provides recovery path from undesired rollout.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Rollback behavior depends on retained revision/state

relationships.mechanism: StatefulSet preserves uniqueness and ordering needed by stateful applications.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Stateless scaling does not require these guarantees

relationships.mechanism: Stateful applications require durable data beyond ephemeral container filesystems.
relationships.effect: Preserves data through container lifecycle events.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Persistence strategy depends on storage backend

relationships.mechanism: DaemonSet ensures a Pod exists on every node or selected subset.
relationships.mathematical_form: one matching Pod per eligible node
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Not appropriate for ordinary replica-based services

relationships.mechanism: Node-wide logging is a cited use case for DaemonSets.
relationships.effect: Places logging agent on relevant nodes.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Central log aggregation remains external/integrated

relationships.mechanism: Ingress controllers are cited as node-dependent DaemonSet workloads.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Exact topology depends on deployment

relationships.mechanism: Storage services are cited as workloads with host/node dependencies.
relationships.effect: Ensures storage agent presence where required.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Storage architecture may use CSI/other patterns

relationships.mechanism: Volumes provide storage beyond the ephemeral container filesystem and can be shared by containers in a Pod.
relationships.effect: Preserves/shared data according to volume type.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Persistence semantics depend on volume backend

relationships.mechanism: Persistent volumes address the loss of container filesystem state on restart.
relationships.effect: Moves durable data outside ephemeral container filesystem.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Ephemeral storage remains appropriate for temporary data

relationships.mechanism: CSI standardizes external storage integration so storage interface code is separated from Kubernetes core.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Backend-specific behavior remains in driver

relationships.mechanism: Container Attached Storage can use Kubernetes extensions such as CRDs to model storage inventory/management.
relationships.effect: Extends Kubernetes object model into storage management.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Not all storage systems use this pattern

relationships.mechanism: ConfigMaps provide configuration to application instances without requiring image rebuilds.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Sensitive data should use Secret

relationships.mechanism: Secrets provide confidential configuration data to Pods.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Source notes Secrets are not encrypted at rest by default

relationships.mechanism: The source explicitly notes additional setup is needed to encrypt Secrets at rest.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Default Secret object is not equivalent to encryption-at-rest

relationships.mechanism: API objects are the record of intent for cluster state.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Current state belongs in status

relationships.mechanism: Status records the current observed state maintained by controllers.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Status is not user intent

relationships.mechanism: Owner references define managing relationships and enable cascading deletion of dependents.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Removing ownership changes lifecycle semantics

relationships.mechanism: CRDs dynamically register custom resource kinds.
relationships.effect: Extends the API without restarting the cluster.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: CRD is schema/registration; custom resource is instance

relationships.mechanism: Custom controllers observe custom resources and reconcile systems toward their declared state.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Controller behavior is implementation-specific

relationships.mechanism: Operator pattern combines custom resources with controllers.
relationships.effect: Turns application operational knowledge into an API/control loop.
relationships.inverse_or_converse: Operator is a pattern, not merely a CRD

relationships.mechanism: Operators use controllers to encode human operational procedures as automation.

source_claims.title: Definition
source_claims.claim: Kubernetes is an open-source container orchestration system for automating deployment, scaling, and management of containerized workloads.

source_claims.title: Cluster model
source_claims.claim: Kubernetes assembles virtual or bare-metal computers into a cluster capable of running container workloads.

source_claims.title: Control-plane/node architecture
source_claims.claim: Kubernetes separates management/control-plane components from worker nodes and exposes resources through an object/API model.

source_claims.title: etcd state store
source_claims.claim: etcd persistently represents cluster configuration/state and favors consistency during network partitions.

source_claims.title: API server
source_claims.claim: The API server exposes the Kubernetes API, validates REST requests, persists API-object state, and participates in watch-driven coordination.

source_claims.title: Scheduler
source_claims.claim: The scheduler matches unscheduled Pods to nodes using resource availability and constraints.

source_claims.title: Controllers
source_claims.claim: Controllers reconcile actual cluster state toward desired state and can replace failed workloads.

source_claims.title: kubelet
source_claims.claim: kubelet maintains Pod/container state on each node and reports node status.

source_claims.title: Runtime_CRi
source_claims.claim: The container runtime manages container lifecycle while CRI decouples kubelet from implementation.

source_claims.title: Networking
source_claims.claim: kube-proxy implements network proxy/load-balancing behavior for Services.

source_claims.title: Namespaces
source_claims.claim: Namespaces segregate Kubernetes resources across teams/projects/environments.

source_claims.title: Pods
source_claims.claim: Pods are the basic deployable unit and group one or more co-located containers with a Pod network identity.

source_claims.title: Workloads
source_claims.claim: Higher-level workload objects declaratively manage Pods, including ReplicaSets, Deployments, StatefulSets and DaemonSets.

source_claims.title: Services
source_claims.claim: Services provide stable IP/DNS identity and load-balance traffic to Pods selected by labels.

source_claims.title: Storage
source_claims.claim: Volumes, persistent storage, Container Attached Storage, and CSI address storage persistence and external storage integration.

source_claims.title: Configuration
source_claims.claim: ConfigMaps and Secrets externalize configuration; Secrets are intended for confidential data and require additional protection for at-rest encryption.

source_claims.title: API objects
source_claims.claim: Kubernetes objects record intent with metadata, spec, status, ownership, and lifecycle semantics.

source_claims.title: Extensions
source_claims.claim: CRDs, custom controllers, and Operators extend Kubernetes declaratively.

source_claims.title: API security
source_claims.claim: TLS, authentication, and authorization mechanisms protect the Kubernetes API.

source_claims.title: Cluster API
source_claims.claim: Cluster API applies Kubernetes object/API principles to infrastructure and machines.

source_claims.title: Uses
source_claims.claim: Kubernetes is used across deployment, scaling, cloud/data-center management, observability, and related infrastructure workflows.

source_claims.title: Complexity/criticism
source_claims.claim: The source discusses complexity, ecosystem fragmentation, operational difficulty, and reasons managed services/PaaS approaches emerged.

source_claims.title: History
source_claims.claim: Kubernetes originated at Google, drew on Borg and Promise Theory, was announced in 2014, and was contributed to CNCF.

source_claims.title: Release timeline
source_claims.claim: The source contains a release/support timeline through Kubernetes 1.36 and related support windows.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: Kubernetes is a virtual machine hypervisor
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: Kubernetes orchestrates workloads; it can run on virtual machines or bare metal but is not itself the VM hypervisor.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: A Pod is just a container
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: A Pod is the deployable unit and can contain one or more co-located containers.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: A Service is a Pod with a stable IP
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: A Service is an abstraction over a selected set of Pods and provides stable network identity.
Scheduler places unscheduled Pods; controllers reconcile resource state and replica counts.
etcd stores cluster state; container runtime executes containers on nodes.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: Secrets are automatically encrypted at rest
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: The source explicitly notes Secrets are not encrypted at rest by default and require additional setup.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: Namespace alone provides full security isolation
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: Namespaces partition resources, while authorization controls API permissions.
StatefulSet provides identity/order orchestration properties; the database remains the application.
kubelet maintains workload state on its node; scheduler selects nodes.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: Reconciliation is a one-time deployment step
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: Controllers continuously drive actual state toward desired state.

misconceptions_and_corrections.misconception: Pod IP is the stable application endpoint
misconceptions_and_corrections.correction: Pods can be replaced; Services provide stable IP/DNS identity.
CRD defines an API resource type; a controller/operator provides behavior.

why_it_matters.core_problem: Coordinate desired software state across changing distributed compute infrastructure without requiring humans to manually orchestrate every machine and recovery action.

major_value_propositions.because: Controllers turn desired-state declarations into repeatable reconciliation loops.
Failure-induced divergence can trigger replacement/recovery actions.
Schedulers and workload controllers coordinate resource supply with workload demand.
A common API/object model abstracts workload management across machines, distributions and cloud environments.
CRDs, controllers, operators, scheduler extensions and CSI allow the platform to be adapted without changing the entire core.
The same declarative state model applies across workloads, networking, storage, configuration and infrastructure.

why_it_matters.central_insight: Kubernetes is best understood as a distributed control system and extensible API platform, not merely as a tool that 'runs containers'.
